_doc: Project anchor for this design system's Figma integration. Single source of truth for which Figma file we read from, and for the identity that generation needs. Maps in maps/*.json resolve their `source` keys against this file. Never hard-code a file key in a script or a skill — read it from here, so pointing the system at a different file is one edit.

bridges._doc: TWO bridges, recorded separately. The READ bridge is the only one anything depends on: the explore -> report -> decide -> build arc completes without the write bridge, and `pnpm verify` is green on a machine with neither Figma Desktop nor a plugin installed — which is what keeps the template's fresh-clone promise intact. The WRITE bridge is opt-in and unwired: no pnpm script, no gate and no CI job invokes it. Code stays canonical for token values in both directions; a difference is drift in Figma, never a change to adopt back.

read._doc: The OFFICIAL Figma MCP connector. No daemon, no plugin, no Figma Desktop. Chosen because everything the arc needs is a READ, and every other bridge adds a local install and a background process that can fail.
read._usedByNote: No skill. Reading the design source is a person's job, done when reference is needed — a scheduled sweep would imply an authority the canvas does not have. The call sequences live in README.md.

write._doc: figma-console MCP driving the Desktop Bridge plugin. OPT-IN: nothing in this repo depends on it. Every write must first compare `figma.fileKey` against sources.<key>.key and pin the target with `figma_navigate({ url, lock: true })` — the active file drifts between open documents, and an unpinned write lands wherever the user last clicked. First exercised against this source on 2026-08-28.
requires: Desktop Bridge plugin open in the target file
local figma-console MCP server (FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN only for the REST-backed tools)
write._gatedNote: NO gate exercises this bridge, so a generated Figma set can drift from its component with nothing failing anywhere. maps/components.json is a record, not a check. This is a known hole and it contradicts the repo's own enforcement rule — a contract whose breach produces no build error has to be gated in CI, or it is enforced on whichever machine happens to run it. Accepted at template stage because nothing has been generated yet; it should not survive contact with a real component library. Read boundVariables back rather than trusting the render: a baked literal and a bound value look identical in any single mode.
write._note20261012: The 2026-10-12 foundations write used the OFFICIAL Figma connector's use_figma tool, not this figma-console bridge. The fileKey was passed explicitly on every call, which removes the drifting-active-file risk described above.

weave.name: Weave
weave.purpose: The design source. Started EMPTY on 2026-10-12, so the flow ran in reverse for the foundations: tokens were authored in code from a brief, then written into this file as variables (5 collections, 139 variables) plus a Foundations specimen page. Code stays canonical for values; a difference here is drift in Figma.
weave._publishedNote: Not published as a library, so component instances have no durable componentKey yet. Until it is published the only join available is pageId + componentSetId, and those are file-local and change. Record them, but treat them as refreshable — see schema/components.schema.json.
weave._previousSource: Until 2026-10-12 this key pointed at the template author's file (eUO2kF0A3tJXdVTcvEPQjW, "weave — Mokkap masterclass"). Everything below was re-measured against the new file; nothing from the old reading carries over.

prefix._doc: Set once in /ds.config.json via `pnpm init-ds <name>`. Repeated here only so a Figma script has one file to read; ds.config.json is authoritative and init-ds rewrites both.
prefix.name: weave

variableNaming._doc: MEASURED 2026-10-12 by live read of the Weave file. A variable's Figma `name` is its DTCG path with `/` separators; `codeSyntax.WEB` is the CSS custom property wrapped in var(). Both were written from code, so they agree by construction — a read that finds otherwise is drift.
variableNaming._separatorNote: Slash-separated groups, one per DTCG nesting level.
knownProblems: Primitives are scoped [] (hidden from pickers) on purpose; roles in Color are what designers bind.
font/line-height/* are unitless multipliers (CSS). Figma line-height variables bind in px, so these are scoped [] and applied as percentages by hand.

font._doc: MEASURED 2026-10-12. Families and sizes exist as variables in the Typography collection; NO text styles exist yet.
knownProblems: No text styles. Type is applied as raw font + size on the specimen page. Create styles before generating components, or every component set bakes in hand-set type.

themes._doc: MEASURED 2026-10-12. The Color collection has Light and Dark modes, by decision (brief: light + dark). Light is the default; code emits Dark under [data-weave-theme='dark'].

variableCollections._doc: Figma collection -> canonical DTCG source file under packages/tokens/tokens/. Filled 2026-10-12 from a live read; maps/tokens.json carries the per-variable correspondence.

variantConventions._doc: A Figma variant property value must match the component's prop value exactly, or the two surfaces describe different components. The canon lives in .ai/maps/prop-map.md §1 and packages/contracts/prop-canon.json — THOSE ARE AUTHORITATIVE; this is a pointer, not a copy.
variantConventions.propertyCase: TitleCase property name, prop-exact value — Hierarchy=secondary, Size=m
variantConventions.statesAreNotVariants: Hover / Pressed / Focused are runtime states the browser owns. They must not become a variant property that maps to a prop. See .ai/maps/proposals/README.md.

codePathConvention._doc: A Figma component reconciles against its CONTRACT, not against a framework implementation. Component source is generated into a consumer's repository and is not in this repo at all, so there is nothing here for it to point at.
